page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m2.xlarge is a burstable virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache. The system is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers, reflecting its burstable design. Single-core and multi-core CPU tests via stress-ng and Geekbench register in the weak (bottom 25%) to poor (bottom 10%) categories, with a Geekbench single-core score of 889.0 and a multi-core score of 2603.0. Memory bandwidth is similarly constrained, with read-only large block transfers at 30.76 GB/sec (weak) and write large block transfers at 27.25 GB/sec (average). Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, also score in the bottom 10%.

As a burstable instance, the ecs.t5-c1m2.xlarge offers a highly cost-efficient profile for workloads that do not require continuous high CPU utilization. The primary tradeoff is the CPU credit system inherent to burstable instances; sustained heavy computations will deplete credits, leading to throttled performance. This resource density makes it an economical choice for baseline operations but unsuitable for sustained high-throughput tasks.

This instance is best suited for low-traffic web serving, lightweight database operations, development or testing environments, and small-scale microservices. Its benchmarked static web serving throughput of 3.14 GB/sec and Redis SET performance of 4.55 million operations per second confirm its viability for non-critical, bursty application workloads rather than intensive data processing or large-scale LLM inference.
